_what: Which reference page each live Trillion MCP tool is documented on, in the order a person meets them, plus a short opening for each page and hand-written example arguments where a made-up value reads better than a placeholder. Every tool in the live tools/list must appear exactly once; make-reference.mjs refuses otherwise.

groups.title: Setup and goals
groups.description: Start Trillion with a new person and keep what they are working toward.
groups.intro: These tools get a person started and keep what they are working toward. Every decision is weighed against these goals, so your AI reads them before it advises.

groups.title: Decisions
groups.description: Walk a decision through its questions, record the choice, and learn from how it turned out.
groups.intro: A decision starts with a goal, the facts so far and at least two options. Your AI then answers one question at a time until none remain, records the choice with its reason, next action and how you will know it worked, and later reports how it went. On the free plan a decision is not kept after it is made; a paid plan keeps every decision, note and result.

groups.title: Messages and activity
groups.description: Keep conversations word for word so every AI you use can read them, and see what your AIs did.
groups.intro: Everything you say to one AI can be read by every other AI you connect. These tools keep conversations, bring in earlier chats from an export, and show what each AI did and why.

groups.title: Marketplace tools
groups.description: Find a tool that does the job, run it, build your own and offer it to others.
groups.intro: The Marketplace holds everything your AI can use, yours and everyone's. A tool does one job: transcribe a recording, cut a video, call a web service. Your AI finds one by describing the job in plain words, runs it, and asks you whether it did the job; every run is listed in Runs. When no tool fits, your AI can build one, keep it under Yours, and publish it for everyone. Running tools from the Marketplace comes with a paid plan.

groups.title: Workflows
groups.description: Get a job done in several checked steps, and keep your own step-by-step methods.
groups.intro: A workflow is a job done in several steps, where each step's result is checked before the next one starts. Your AI does most steps itself; a step that names a Marketplace tool is run by Trillion. You can keep your own workflows, for example from a checklist you already follow.

groups.title: Rules, schedules and connected accounts
groups.description: Make Trillion run a tool or workflow by itself when something happens or at a set time.
groups.intro: Rules and schedules run a tool or start a workflow with no AI in the loop: a rule when something happens (a message is recorded, a comment arrives, something is added to a shared space), a schedule at a time. Connected accounts, such as your Instagram, are where outside events come from.

groups.title: Files and media
groups.description: Save, find, read and show your files, and find moments in your recordings.
groups.intro: Your files live in your Trillion, where any AI you connect can find, read and show them. Big files are sent in pieces or straight from a computer. What an AI works out about a file, like a transcript or a summary, is kept so no AI has to work it out again. Files come with a paid plan.

groups.title: Hand off work
groups.description: Let the AIs you use find each other and hand work on, on your account or inside a shared space.
groups.intro: Each AI you connect can say what it does, find the others, and hand them a job. The job waits until an agent takes it, and the agent that handed it off reads the result. The same works inside a shared space, where every member sees the handoff. Handing work between your AI apps comes with a paid plan.

groups.title: Shared spaces
groups.description: Work with other people in a group, project or event: invite them, share into it, and decide who may do what.
groups.intro: A shared space is a group, project, event, community or one-to-one you work in with other people. It holds only what members put there; nobody, and no agent, can read another member's private Trillion through it. Spaces come with a paid plan.

groups.title: Sharing
groups.description: Choose who sees each thing you keep, where the things you send to Trillion go, and read what others shared with you.
groups.intro: Every record you keep, a goal, a decision, a message, a file or a tool, can be shared with the Trillion network, a shared space or particular people, or kept to yourself. These tools read and change those choices, and set where the pages and files you send to Trillion go.

groups.title: People and introductions
groups.description: Find people on the Trillion network who offer what you need, and ask to meet them.
groups.intro: The Trillion network finds people by what they offer and what they are looking for. Contact details are shared only when both people agree to meet. Trillion's network comes with a paid plan.

groups.title: Communities
groups.description: Join a community, post, go to events, take courses and meet other members.
groups.intro: A community is a shared space with its own rules for who may join, a feed of posts, events, courses, levels and rewards. A community never shares anyone's contact. Its owner can change how it works and let members be paired to meet each other.

groups.title: Book a session
groups.description: See the sessions you can book with a person, pay, pick a time, and move or cancel it.
groups.intro: Some sessions are with a person, for example working a decision through together. These tools show what is on offer, keep the time you pick while you pay, book it on the host's calendar, and move or cancel it.

groups.title: Writing
groups.description: Write in your own formats, and keep private answers to the questions your audience asks.
groups.intro: Your content formats say how you write each kind of piece, from a newsletter to a short video. The audience question tools keep questions people ask in public, check them against their sources, and keep a private draft answer. Nothing here is published.

groups.title: Lists, sidebar and screen
groups.description: Keep lists, arrange the sidebar and screen, and show the person tours and looks.
groups.intro: These tools change what the person sees in Trillion: their lists and the rows in them, the sidebar, screen layouts, guided tours and screen looks, and a Trillion screen drawn right in the chat.

groups.title: Posts, links and what was sent
groups.description: Draft, check, approve and publish posts, keep a link-in-bio page, publish insights and see everything sent.
groups.intro: These tools put the person's words out in the world only after they approve them: posts to their connected accounts, their link-in-bio page, insights they approved, and a record of everything their AIs sent.

groups.title: Public apps and source projects
groups.description: Publish small public apps with visitor actions, connect domains, and edit a connected GitHub project's source.
groups.intro: These tools publish a public app (its pages and the actions visitors can take), install it in the account or a space, connect a domain, read responses and visits, and change a connected GitHub project's source at an exact revision.
